title: One flat model computes all six etale/pro-etale scalar cube faces
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $a:A\to B$ any homomorphism of discrete commutative rings. Use constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the fixed small etale and pro-etale sites, and their ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $R=A,B$, let $l_R^0,p_R^0,C_Z^{R,0}$ denote ordinary etale pullback along $f$, ordinary pro-etale pullback along $f$, and comparison inverse image along $\nu_Z$ ($Z=X,Y$), with canonical constant-coefficient identifications [def-kun-projection-formula-map, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $l_R,p_R,C_Z^R$ for their exact derived functors, and $E_Z^t=B_Z\otimes_{A_Z}-$, $T_Z^t=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ for ordinary and derived scalar extension ($t=e,p$) [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $d_R^0:p_R^0C_Y^{R,0}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_X^{R,0}l_R^0$ be the ordinary canonical square and $d_R$ its exact localization [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Let $c^{e,0},c^{p,0},\delta_Z^0$ be the ordinary scalar/pullback comparisons with directions $l_B^0E_Y^e\to E_X^el_A^0$, $p_B^0E_Y^p\to E_X^pp_A^0$, and $E_Z^pC_Z^{A,0}\to C_Z^{B,0}E_Z^e$, respectively, normalized on generalized pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction]. Let $c^e:l_BT_Y^e\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^el_A$ be the specified comparison [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], and let $c^p:p_BT_Y^p\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^pp_A$, $\delta_Z:T_Z^pC_Z^A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z^BT_Z^e$ be the canonical ringed derived scalar/pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons].

Every complex $K$ of $A_Y$-module sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and flat in every degree [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every such $P$, all intermediate ordinary complexes in the two words $p_B^0E_Y^pC_Y^{A,0}P$ and $C_X^{B,0}E_X^el_A^0P$ and the two three-face routes between them are K-flat with flat terms over their current coefficient ring. Successive canonical representative counits $Lh^*Q(P')\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(h^*P')$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], including the identity geometric morphism with structural ring map $a$, identify every vertex of these routes with localization of the ordinary word on this same $P$. Under these vertex identifications the six faces $c^p$, $T_X^p(d_A)$, $\delta_X$, $p_B(\delta_Y)$, $d_B$, $C_X^B(c^e)$ are respectively the localizations of $c^{p,0}$, $E_X^p(d_A^0)$, $\delta_X^0$, $p_B^0(\delta_Y^0)$, $d_B^0$, $C_X^{B,0}(c^{e,0})$, evaluated at their corresponding ordinary inputs. The identifications are natural for chain maps between these resolving complexes. This is a simultaneous face-normalization assertion; it imposes no flatness of $a$, geometric finiteness, or boundedness of $P$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, label lemma-derived-pullback-composition, proof on one common flat-term K-flat representative; with labels lemma-K-flat-resolution, lemma-pullback-K-flat, lemma-derived-base-change, lemma-pullback-tensor-product. Simultaneous normalization of the six specified faces is the agent extraction of old proof steps 3–4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to the small etale site of $Y$ and its constant ring sheaf $A_Y$. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$, with $P$ K-flat and flat in every degree (indeed the map can be taken termwise surjective). Fix any such $P$ for the remaining steps; no special choice of this resolution will be used.

proof.text: Regard $l_R^0,p_R^0,C_Z^{R,0}$ as module pullbacks of their geometric morphisms, with the canonical isomorphisms on constant rings. The inverse-image square and exactness are the first assertion of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]; its later qcqs assertion is not used. Regard $E_Z^t$ as module pullback for the identity geometric morphism with structural map $A_Z\to B_Z$. Thus every letter in either route is a pullback of ringed topoi, including the letters that change coefficients. Apply the preservation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] after each letter, starting at $P$. Induction on the length of the ordinary word shows that every suffix and every full vertex word is K-flat with flat terms over its current ring. This preservation does not assume that $B$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); representative calculation specialized to the scalar/site cube.

proof.text:
For clarity list the six ordinary vertices (all evaluated on $P$):
$$W_0=p_B^0E_Y^pC_Y^{A,0}P,\quad W_1=E_X^pp_A^0C_Y^{A,0}P,\quad W_2=E_X^pC_X^{A,0}l_A^0P,$$
$$W_3=C_X^{B,0}E_X^el_A^0P,\quad W_4=p_B^0C_Y^{B,0}E_Y^eP,\quad W_5=C_X^{B,0}l_B^0E_Y^eP.$$
The paths are $0\to1\to2\to3$ and $0\to4\to5\to3$. For any suffix $W$ of these words define $j_W$ from the corresponding derived word on $Q_AP$ to $Q(W(P))$ recursively. Set $j_{\varnothing}=1$ and
$$j_{hW}=\epsilon_{h,W(P)}\circ Lh^*(j_W),$$
where $h$ is the ringed morphism for the next letter. The counit and its naturality are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Step 2 checks precisely its K-flat and flat-term hypotheses, so every $j_W$ is invertible. For the scalar letters this is the derived extension of scalars and its counit [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For the exact geometric letters, the exact localization is a left derived functor with its localization comparison as counit [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Hence these are the successive canonical representative identifications of the statement, including at the two common endpoints.

proof.text: The square map $d_R$ is, by [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], the exact localization of $d_R^0$. Consequently, using the geometric-letter identifications of Step 3, its component at $QN$ is $Q(d_{R,N}^0)$ for every ordinary complex $N$. This applies to $N=P$ for $R=A$, and to $N=E_Y^eP$ for $R=B$. For the latter face the actual input is $T_Y^eQ_AP$; naturality of $d_B$ along the scalar representative isomorphism $T_Y^eQ_AP\to Q_BE_Y^eP$ gives the same formula. Thus the unwhiskered site-square faces have their required ordinary representatives.

proof.text: We next check $c^p$ and $\delta_Z$ on their two-letter inputs. For each one, the two orders of coefficient extension and geometric pullback are composites of ringed morphisms with the same underlying geometric inverse image. Their structural ring maps agree: under the constant-ring identifications both send a local constant $a$ to its image in $B$. The normalized lifts of all these ringed morphisms, and of their composites, are those recorded by the System of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]; by [def-sfb-ringed-derived-comparison-data] a System records a lift for every morphism together with its Composition and TwoIso comparisons, so no further existence of lifts is needed. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-composition-comparison] to each path, and [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-two-iso-comparison] to the specified identity geometric isomorphism between the resulting composites. These nodes give ordinary and derived comparisons with the flat-term K-flat representative formulas. Cancelling their common single-pullback representative identifies the derived path comparison with the localization of the ordinary path comparison under the $j$'s. The ordinary comparison in the direction $h_B^0E\to Eh_A^0$ sends the pulled-back scalar insertion $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes h_A^0m$; its inverse is used for $\delta_Z^0$. These are exactly the generalized pure-tensor normalizations stipulated in the statement, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between the two composites. The canonical ringed comparisons [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] are these composition/transport comparisons. Therefore $c^p$ and $\delta_Z$ have representatives $c^{p,0}$ and $\delta_Z^0$, respectively. The argument applies to $C_Y^{A,0}P$ and to $l_A^0P$ as needed, by Step 2.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); representative calculation specialized to the scalar/site cube.

proof.text:
For the etale face use the specified normalization, not an unspecified derived isomorphism. In [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso] substitute the chosen $P$ into
$$c^e_{Q_AP};T_X^e(g_{A,P});r_{l_A^0P}=l_B(r_P);g_{B,E_Y^eP};Q_B(c^{e,0}_P).$$
Here $g$ and $r$ are the geometric and scalar representative counits. They are precisely the two successive factors defining $j_{E_X^el_A^0}$ and $j_{l_B^0E_Y^e}$ in Step 3. Their invertibility was established there. Consequently the displayed defining equation says exactly that the conjugate of $c^e_{Q_AP}$ by those two $j$'s is $Q_B(c^{e,0}_P)$. Its ordinary comparison $a_P$ equals $c^{e,0}_P$. Indeed $a$ is the conjugate of the sectionwise identity $\mathrm{Res}\,f_{B,*}=f_{A,*}\mathrm{Res}$, so it carries the unit of the composite adjunction $f_B^*E_Y\dashv\mathrm{Res}\,f_{B,*}$ to that of $E_Xf_A^*\dashv f_{A,*}\mathrm{Res}$. Evaluated on a local section $m$, the first unit is $m\mapsto$ the pulled-back insertion of $1\otimes m$, the second is $m\mapsto1\otimes(\text{pulled-back }m)$. Hence $a_P$ sends the pulled-back $1\otimes m$ to $1\otimes f_A^0m$, and by $B_X$-linearity it sends $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes f_A^0m$ on generalized pure tensors. That is the normalization defining $c^{e,0}$; since such tensors generate after sheafification, the two $B_X$-linear maps coincide. No uniqueness of an unnormalized isomorphism is being assumed.

proof.text:
The face computations remain valid with their outer letters. Indeed, suppose $\alpha:L(U)\to L(V)$ has ordinary representative $\alpha^0:U^0(P)\to V^0(P)$, meaning $j_V\alpha=Q(\alpha^0)j_U$. Apply a derived outer letter $Lh^*$ and then its representative counit. Naturality of that counit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] gives
$$j_{hV}\,Lh^*(\alpha)=Q(h^0\alpha^0)\,j_{hU}.$$
All counits here are invertible by Step 2. Apply this identity to the outer scalar letter $E_X^p$ on $d_A$, to the outer geometric letter $p_B^0$ on $\delta_Y$, and to the outer geometric letter $C_X^{B,0}$ on $c^e$. Together with Steps 4–6 this gives, in the order of the statement, the representatives $c^{p,0}$, $E_X^p(d_A^0)$, $\delta_X^0$, $p_B^0(\delta_Y^0)$, $d_B^0$, and $C_X^{B,0}(c^{e,0})$. The $j_{W_i}$ used here were fixed once in Step 3, so the identifications at a vertex shared by two faces are the same.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); representative calculation specialized to the scalar/site cube.

proof.text: For a chain map $v:P\to P'$ between flat-term K-flat resolving complexes, naturality of each counit gives $j_W(P')\,W^{\mathrm{der}}(Qv)=Q(W^0v)\,j_W(P)$, by induction on the word length in Step 3. The ordinary comparison maps and all six derived comparisons are natural, so their representative equations commute with these chain maps as well. This proves the asserted naturality and simultaneous normalization. The proof only used smallness of the fixed sites, flat-term K-flatness of the representatives, and the ringed structural maps; it used no boundedness of $P$, no finiteness of $f$, and no flatness of $A\to B$.
